Current subtitle: Evac+Chair 1-310 Comfy Seat for Evac+Chairs
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Evac+Chair Comfy Seat is an evacuation chair seat cushion that clips onto the seat frame of an Evac+Chair 300H, 500H, or 600H to give the passenger extra comfort and support during an evacuation down the stairs. It has a molded base and a detachable cushion with integrated leg straps.
It makes the evac chair suit passengers who need more support than the standard seat gives: people of greater girth, people with prosthetic legs, leg calipers, or leg amputations, people in plaster casts, and patients before or after surgery on the hip or femur. That makes it a useful addition to any evacuation chair for disabled passengers, and it can be added to a chair you already own.
Fit: Clips onto the seat frame of the Evac+Chair 300H, 500H, and 600H evacuation chairs
Retrofit: Can be added to an Evac+Chair you already have; simple to fit
Base: Molded base for support
Cushion: Detachable cushion for comfort
Leg Straps: Integrated leg straps help hold the passenger in place
Who It Helps: Passengers of greater girth; people with prosthetic legs, leg calipers, or leg amputations; people in plaster casts; and patients with pre-operative or post-operative hip or femur conditions
Available Models and Options
1-310 – Comfy Seat: Clip-on seat cushion for the Evac+Chair 300H, 500H, and 600H
[H2] Applications
The Comfy Seat suits buildings where an Evac+Chair may need to carry people who cannot sit comfortably or safely on the standard seat.
Typical applications include:
Hospitals, especially orthopedic, surgical, and rehabilitation units
Nursing homes, senior living, and care facilities
Offices, schools, and public buildings with staff or visitors who use prosthetics or have limited mobility
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
Which evacuation chairs does the Comfy Seat fit?
The Comfy Seat clips onto the seat frame of the Evac+Chair 300H, 500H, and 600H. It can be bought with a new chair or added later.
Who is the Comfy Seat for?
It is for passengers who need extra support on an evacuation chair: people of greater girth, people with prosthetic legs, leg calipers, or leg amputations, people in plaster casts, and patients before or after hip or femur surgery.
Does the Comfy Seat turn an Evac+Chair into a bariatric stair chair?
No. It adds comfort and support for passengers of greater girth, but the weight capacity of the chair stays the same (400 lbs for the 300H and 600H).
[H2] About Evac+Chair Evacuation Chairs
Evac+Chair makes stair evacuation chairs, powered stair chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories for moving people with limited mobility on stairs, in an emergency or every day.
The Evac+Chair line includes:
Emergency evacuation chairs: The 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs
Powered stair climbing chairs: The battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 for going up and down the stairs
Stair transport seat: The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat for two-person transport up and down the stairs
Evacuation sleds and mats: The Evac+Sled, Ulti-Mat, and Evac+Sheet rescue sheet
Accessories: Comfy Seat, transfer seat, storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood
[H2] About Evac+Chair
Evac+Chair has made stairway evacuation chairs since 1982, and its chairs were designed in the United States. Explore the full line of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
Keywords: as Ricky noted, the seat cushion terms have no search volume, so the copy is written for the use case (greater girth, prostheses, leg calipers, amputees, plaster casts, and hip or femur conditions), with the product name in the H1 and meta title. The primary keyword "evacuation chair seat cushion" is in the subtitle, first sentence, and meta description. "Evac chair" is in the second intro paragraph, and "evacuation chair for disabled" passengers is in the same paragraph.
Bariatric: Ricky listed "bariatric stair chair" (50) as a secondary keyword. The Comfy Seat helps passengers of greater girth but does not raise the chair's weight capacity, so I used the term only in an honest FAQ ("Does the Comfy Seat turn an Evac+Chair into a bariatric stair chair? No."), as we did with "evacuation wheelchair" on the 600H. Is that OK?
Fit: the Evac+Chair brochures say the Comfy Seat fits the 300H, 500H, and 600H. We sell the 300H and 600H (the 500H is not on Anchortex), so the 500H is mentioned only because it is part of the manufacturer's fit list. Would you like it left out?
Specs: Evac+Chair publishes no size, weight, or warranty for the Comfy Seat. The variant weight is 10 lbs. Is that right?
Spelling: Evac+Chair writes "leg callipers" (British spelling). I used the US spelling, "leg calipers."
Duplicate content: our current description is the Evac+Chair paragraph word for word. The new copy is fully rewritten.
Images: the 2 current Evac+Chair images are kept (1214×783).
Price: $319 with compare-at $425 (75%). No change made.
